title: US August durable goods orders 0.0% vs -0.4% expected
description: Prior was +1.1% Ex-transport +0.3% vs +0.6% expected Prior ex-transport +0.4% Ex-defense +0.1% vs +1.3% prior Non-defense capital goods orders ex-air +1.6% vs +0.5% expected Prior +0.2% The big data point this week was the S&P Global PMI that showed an accelerating US economy. The headline here is flat but the core orders matter much more of the underlying direction of the economy and that's a great number that helps to back up the bullish view on the economy. The market reaction has been nil but this is another brick in the hawkish pyramid. This article was written by Adam Button at inves

title: USTR's Greer: We have reached agreements with China on a sub-set of goods we can trade
description: Speaking on CNBC, Greer said the US will release on Monday the details of negotiations between China and the US. I wouldn't expect to be overwhelmed but at least it's all on the rails. Meanwhile Trump is tweeting. It seems we're at the stage of his Presidency, where he's all about re-naming things. Very productive meeting with President Xi for both the U.S.A. and China. Tremendous things will be happening. title: September final UMich consumer sentiment 48.1 vs 47.6 expected
description: Prelim was 47.8 Prior was 51.7 Current conditions 50.9 vs 50.9 prelim (51.9 prior) Expectations 46.3 vs 45.8 prelim (51.5 prior) One-year inflation expectations 4.6% vs 4.6% prelim (prior 4.0%) Five-year inflation expectations 3.4% vs 3.4% prelim (prior 3.4%) These 'beat' the consensus but these are thinly-forecast indicators so the prelim numbers are a better metric to go by. There was a slight improvement on the headline and expectations but the inflation numbers -- more important right now -- stayed high.
